If you have ADHD and fall apart every month before your period - there is a biological reason you might want to know .

Nearly half of women with ADHD report PMDD. Here’s what’s actually happening underneath. 📌 Sources below.

🌙 Did you know your cycle was hitting your neurodivergent brain differently - or did you spend years thinking it was just you?

author: Feminine Mastery
transcript: I'm going to famsplain neurodivergence and your cycle to you. Stay with me. And this is not comprehensive. There is so much to say here. But let's start with the thing that most neurodivergent women have never been told. Nearly half of women with ADHD report PMDD. Not PMS, PMDD, clinically significant mood collapse every single month. In the general population, it's 28 percent. So if you have a neurodivergent brain and you've been falling apart every month before your period and wondering why it's so much worse for you than it seems to be for everyone else, if you had a woman, now you have a number. And here is why. ADHD is a dopamine difference. Your brain already doesn't regulate dopamine the way a neurotypical brain does. And estrogen runs dopamine. So when estrogen drops in your luteal phase for a neurotypical brain, that's a mood shift, maybe some irritability, some heaviness. For a neurodivergent brain, the dopamine that was already running low just dropped through the floor. Executive function gone. The task that was manageable last week can't start it. Emotional regulation, the thing you've worked so hard to build, barely here. Rejection sensitivity through the roof, everything too loud, too much, too fast. And you've been calling that a personal flaw. You've been adding more system, trying harder, apologizing more, wondering why everyone else seems to cope. And you just don't. And here is what most women don't know. Most neurodivergent women with this pattern spend years in therapy, treated for anxiety, treated for depression, medicated for the symptoms while the cycle went completely unseen underneath. Dr. Lotte Borg-Skoglund, psychiatrist and researcher at the Karolinska Institute in Sweden. She's one of the leading voices on ADHD and female hormones. She says most of these women were being treated for everything except the right thing because nobody mapped the dopamine to the cycle. Nobody said your brain is wired differently and your hormones hit it differently. And those two things together are what's been making the flaw disappear every month. That's not a character flaw. That's not inconsistency. That's not you being too much. That's a neurodivergent brain in a cycling body and the two things talk to each other in a way nobody ever told you about.
title: Why ADHD Women Crash Before Their Period
one_liner: Estrogen regulates dopamine, so when it drops in the luteal phase, ADHD brains lose executive function dramatically.
key_points: Nearly 50% of women with ADHD report PMDD, vs. 28% in the general population
ADHD is a dopamine-regulation difference, and estrogen directly drives dopamine levels
When estrogen drops in the luteal phase, already-low dopamine crashes further — wiping executive function and emotional regulation
Most affected women were treated for anxiety or depression for years while the hormone-cycle link went undiagnosed
